issues.summary: A single non-numeric placeholder turns a numeric column into text, giving lexical min/max and no mean/median/stdev.
Re-raised exceptions do not chain the original error ('raise ... from').

blinding_guess.why: B has a test suite including a stdlib-only check and a dedicated UsageError/exit-code convention, which looks like spec-driven structure, while A is a feature-rich single script with no tests.

notes: Both are single-file, stdlib-only CLIs that compute all six stats, filter, select columns and export JSON; neither has security findings (bandit is empty for both, and there is no eval, shell or network use). A prints a text table by default and emits JSON only with -o (use '-o -' for stdout); B always emits JSON. P13 first failed on both because my probe used sys.stdlib_module_names, which Python 3.9.6 lacks; I replaced it with an explicit allowlist and re-ran. B's tests were run with 'python3 -m unittest' because pytest is not installed. P26 checks a design expectation (numeric stats despite a placeholder value), so I rated it low severity.
